note: Two lenses. 'stated' = what All In Capital says publicly (see data/fund/public_thesis.json for sources). 'revealed' = what the fund's own 12 deal memos and partner notes show it actually rewards. Kushal: 'tell me which one you used and why' -> every verdict shows both, recommendation is driven by 'revealed', and any disagreement between lenses is printed.
scale: Each criterion 0-5. Weighted to 0-10 per lens. A criterion with no evidence is scored as missing_value (it drags the score, it is never skipped) and lowers coverage.
pedigree_rule: Credentials alone (IIT, PhD, ex-FAANG, ex-founder) cannot lift any criterion above pedigree_cap. Score the evidence, not the pedigree. (Partner notes, Meeting 3: 'credentials are not a business'.)

revealed.description: Reconstructed from the 12 deal memos (6 invested, 6 passed) and 5 partner meetings. Founder behaviour is scored separately from path to market, as agreed in Meeting 3.

criteria.name: Founders own the defining risk
criteria.definition: Every business has one risk that kills it: credit/default for a lender, the regulator for drones/aviation/crypto, repeat rate for a brand, profitability-at-density for ops-heavy models. Score whether the founders treat that risk as theirs to manage, with a plan, rather than someone else's problem.
criteria.high: Names the risk unprompted and shows what they are doing about it (credit-risk hire plan, regulator milestone sequence, cohort data, contribution-margin path).
criteria.low: Delegates the risk ('the NBFC handles defaults', 'solved once the tech works', 'rules will get friendlier', 'needs a big raise to reach density').
criteria.intake_observability: partial - decks rarely show it; form answers about risks/'what would make you quit' do. Full test is on the call.

criteria.name: Went to the customer first
criteria.definition: Evidence the founders did unscalable, on-the-ground work with real customers before building or scaling: manual operations, field visits, hand-run transactions, pilots treated as learning.
criteria.high: Specific customer sites, named pilots, store/farm/user visits, what broke and what they changed.
criteria.low: Product built around an assumption; traction is downloads/followers; no customer conversations described.
criteria.intake_observability: good - decks and forms usually describe how the first customers were found.

criteria.name: Earned traction on the metric that matters
criteria.definition: Traction measured on the sector's deciding metric (see sector_key_metrics), and earned rather than bought. A missing deciding metric is scored as missing_value.
criteria.high: Cohort repeat / retention / default data / live-site pilot results given with numbers; growth not mostly paid.
criteria.low: Vanity metrics only (downloads, followers, GMV with no margin); growth mostly paid; deciding metric absent.
criteria.intake_observability: good - either the number is in the application or it is not.

criteria.name: Credible path to market
criteria.definition: Who pays, how the product reaches them, and what stands in the way (regulation, liability, procurement cycles) - with a concrete sequence. Scored separately from founder quality.
criteria.high: Paying or signed customer, regulator-facing plan with milestones, liability addressed, channel proven.
criteria.low: No paying customer identified; regulatory path absent; market size asserted rather than evidenced.
precedents: ePlane (invested despite long path, because the sequence was clear)

criteria.name: Works on a pre-seed cheque
criteria.definition: Can the company reach its next proof point with the capital a pre-seed fund deploys, without becoming the small cheque that gets diluted or squeezed when larger funds set terms?
criteria.high: Capital-efficient, milestones reachable with the ask; or long-duration but cheque sized to survive a slow path.
criteria.low: Only works at density/scale that needs far more capital than the fund deploys; negative contribution margin with no niche.
precedents: ePlane (invested, cheque sized for slow path)

criteria.name: Travels beyond the founder
criteria.definition: Is there something that keeps working and gets harder to copy as it scales (field execution, network, data, distribution), or is the product the founder's personal talent/audience?
criteria.high: Defensibility the founder can articulate and examine; process or network that does not depend on one person.
criteria.low: Product is the founder (one teacher, one influencer); defensive when asked about copycats.
precedents: SuperK (invested: field execution hard to copy)

stated.description: What All In Capital says publicly (fund site, apply page, Fund II launch coverage, Kushal Bhagia's interviews and posts). Every criterion cites its sources; full quotes in data/fund/public_thesis.json.

criteria.name: In a focus sector
criteria.definition: Fund II is sector-agnostic with special focus on consumer tech, deeptech, fintech and consumer brands; intended mix ~50% consumer, ~30% Indian AI, ~20% deeptech. Vertical AI (one industry) preferred over horizontal; thin API wrappers seen as weakly defensible.
criteria.high: Squarely in a focus sector, or vertical AI with a real industry problem.
criteria.low: Outside the focus sectors with no AI/consumer/deeptech angle, or a thin wrapper.

criteria.name: Stage and round the fund can lead
criteria.definition: Paper-plan through MVP to early paying customers; first cheque USD 200-600K (INR 3-5 Cr in Fund II), leading or co-leading rounds up to roughly INR 6 Cr, usually on a convertible note. Not a fit for revenue-generating companies where large VCs compete.
criteria.high: First institutional round the fund can lead at its cheque size.
criteria.low: Series A / large round, or already institutionally funded with big VCs competing.

criteria.name: Founder-market fit and earned secrets
criteria.definition: The core public lens: what the founders know and can or cannot do for this opportunity; the key skills needed and the key risk; 'earned secrets'; proven ability to build (shipped product, handled scale); loving the problem enough to stay 5-6 years; long shared history between co-founders.
criteria.high: Founders with demonstrated, specific knowledge of this problem and a record of building; complementary team with history.
criteria.low: No evidence of insight or ability to build specific to this problem.

criteria.name: Non-obvious, ambitious opportunity
criteria.definition: Backs non-obvious founders and non-consensus ideas, a vision that inspires, ambition beyond the first market (global exposure valued); does not follow what is hot.
criteria.high: A non-consensus insight with a large or global ambition.
criteria.low: A me-too in a crowded, hot category; local ambition only.

other: the metric the founder says proves demand

gates.name: Portfolio conflict
gates.rule: Overlaps an existing portfolio company (same customer + same job). Checked against the full portfolio list, not memory. Default is no; a false alarm is preferred to a miss (Meeting 4).
gates.effect: HOLD_CONFLICT - Kushal speaks to the portfolio founder before anything else.

gates.name: Exists only if the rules change
gates.rule: The business depends on a favourable regulatory change to exist (Coinlane). Category decision, not a people decision.
gates.effect: PASS suggested; Kushal still sees it.

gates.name: Sector label stretch
gates.rule: Fits a stated sector only by label (rural credit, 'fintech' that is really lending ops). Not a reject: Jai Kisan precedent - founder behaviour mattered more than the label.

gates.name: Outside mandate
gates.rule: Round or stage the fund cannot lead at its cheque size: public statements say it leads/co-leads first rounds up to roughly INR 6 Cr with USD 200-600K cheques and is not a fit for revenue-generating companies where large VCs compete (Series A and later).
gates.effect: PASS suggested on mandate, not on the company; Kushal still sees it.

routing.note: Thresholds fixed before running the batch or the backtest. Below screen_first -> PASS with 'what would change our view'. Every outcome goes to Kushal; nothing is auto-advanced or auto-rejected.

rule_history.rule: PASS whenever revealed < 4.5 or G2 fires.

A score-based PASS also requires R1 (founders own the defining risk) to be evidenced with medium or high confidence; otherwise the application is routed to SCREEN_FIRST. Gate-based passes (G2, G4) are unchanged. Reason: in the blind backtest the only investment marked 'pass' (ePlane) and every investment in the no-founder variant were cases where founder behaviour was not observable. This is the breach response written into the trust contract ('system may not suggest pass' without founder evidence). Thresholds were not retuned.
